title: Learning Low-Order Approximations of the Quark Propagator in Lattice QCD
summary: The hopping expansion is an important approximation of the quark propagator in lattice quantum chromodynamics, but it diverges for light quarks, which limits the scope of strong-coupling and finite-density simulations. We present an artificial scientific discovery framework using gauge-equivariant neural networks in the Clifford basis to extract interpretable approximations. Our approach yields improved low-order approximations that outperform the hopping expansion at identical computational cost. In the parameter regime where the hopping expansion fails, our approach identifies convergent behavior, thus suggesting a novel series expansion. The discovered approximations generalize to unseen gauge fields and volumes, enabling immediate implementation as plug-in replacements and a new theoretical understanding of quark-propagator expansions.

AI.tldr: Researchers used gauge-equivariant neural networks to develop an improved approximation method for the quark propagator in lattice QCD, which surpasses the traditional hopping expansion in accuracy and remains effective even where the hopping expansion fails. This new method also suggests a novel series expansion and can be applied to different gauge fields and volumes.
AI.motivation: The motivation behind this paper is to address the limitations of the hopping expansion, particularly its divergence for light quarks, which hinders strong-coupling and finite-density simulations in lattice QCD. The authors aim to find a more reliable and efficient approximation that can handle these challenging cases and improve upon the existing methods without increasing computational costs.
AI.method: The method involves employing an artificial scientific discovery framework that utilizes gauge-equivariant neural networks within the Clifford basis. This approach is designed to learn and extract interpretable approximations of the quark propagator, with the goal of identifying a convergent behavior even in parameter regimes where the standard hopping expansion does not work.
AI.result: The results show that the proposed low-order approximations are superior to the hopping expansion when the computational cost is kept the same. Moreover, the new method successfully identifies convergent behavior in scenarios where the hopping expansion diverges, indicating the potential for a new type of series expansion. Additionally, the approximations derived from the method are found to be generalizable across different gauge fields and volumes.
AI.conclusion: The conclusion of the paper highlights that the new approximation method not only provides a practical solution by acting as a plug-in replacement for the current techniques but also offers a fresh theoretical perspective on quark-propagator expansions. It opens up possibilities for further research and application in the field of lattice QCD, especially concerning light quarks and at high densities or strong couplings.
